pathway.title: Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The first finding is revenue durability. Kodiak sells compression on fixed monthly fees under primary terms of one to seven years, with 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and its compression remaining performance obligations were USD 2,643.2 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 1,632.9 million at March 31, 2026, with 49.9% falling in 2028 or later (Documentary Fact, from the business-context handoff). The mechanism is that fixed fees turn 98.2% utilisation into revenue largely independent of volume, so contracted obligations of 2.17 times LTM compression revenue protect near-term coverage of debt service. The implication is stronger revenue visibility than the previous quarter showed, tempered because the filings do not explain the jump and the month-to-month tail would reprice quickly in a weak basin.

The second is financial risk and leverage. Total debt was USD 2,780.9 million, or 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA of USD 766.1 million, and net debt was 3.45x, against 4.31x total and 4.30x net at FY2024 and 3.66x total at FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Calculated in the financial-base handoff). The mechanism is that the May equity offering of USD 836.1 million arrived in the same period as the USD 576.0 million cash acquisition and a notes refinancing, so debt rose by USD 166.3 million since December 2025 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 51.1 million. The implication for leverage tolerance is a stepped-down but not yet clearly falling ratio; the figure overstates leverage on a full-year perimeter because EBITDA from the acquired power business before April 1, 2026 is Not calculable, and management's covenant-basis ratio of 3.2x (Management Language) cannot be recomputed.

The third is funding and liquidity. Liquidity was USD 1,742.0 million (cash of USD 137.6 million and undrawn ABL capacity of USD 1,604.5 million, an upper bound because the borrowing base is not supplied), against purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion, of which USD 587.9 million is expected within twelve months, up from USD 276.4 million at March 31, 2026. Revised 2026 guidance implies discretionary cash flow less growth and other capital spending of negative USD 235.0 million to negative USD 125.0 million, before dividends of about USD 49.5 million a quarter. The mechanism is that the spending is discretionary in timing but contractually committed once ordered, and the ABL, which matures September 5, 2030 and is secured on essentially all assets, is the funding backstop. The implication is that refinancing risk is low through 2029 but that net leverage, on the indicative sensitivity below, ends 2026 at about 3.27x to 3.52x, roughly where it is today, unless adjusted EBITDA beats guidance or equity is raised again (Analyst Interpretation).

The fourth is earnings and cash quality. Add-backs were USD 162.7 million, or 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA, and unadjusted leverage on the same debt would be 4.61x; operating cash flow was 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA against 83.9% in FY2025, as working capital used USD 154.6 million in the first half (Documentary Fact and Calculated). The mechanism is that equity compensation, a settled sales tax reserve and refinancing and acquisition costs sit outside adjusted EBITDA while the sales tax settlement and working capital absorbed cash. The implication is that adjusted-EBITDA coverage of 4.14x on cash interest paid is a ceiling on debt-service capacity, and monitoring should use operating cash flow.

The fifth is the power transition and ownership. The acquisition closed April 1, 2026 with fair value of consideration of USD 726.4 million (signing value was about USD 675.0 million, logged as a conflict, not reconciled), goodwill of USD 344.8 million on a preliminary allocation, one disclosed lease agreement whose initial term ends April 1, 2028, and no sponsor, since EQT affiliates sold their entire stake by December 2, 2025 (Documentary Fact). The mechanism is that equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, and no sponsor is documented as available to cure a shortfall. The implication is that the next two to three quarters of power contract announcements and utilisation are the main evidence that will move the credit view either way.

runs.text: Strengths. Contracted revenue visibility is the first: fixed-fee compression contracts, 98.2% utilisation, performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, and customer cost pass-throughs for fuel and taxes (Documentary Fact; business-context handoff). Margin resilience is the second: compression adjusted gross margin was 70.0% in the second quarter and adjusted EBITDA margin was 55.4% (Documentary Fact; financial-base handoff), which cushions a revenue decline. Liquidity and maturity profile is the third: USD 1,742.0 million of liquidity, no scheduled maturity of size before the ABL in 2030, and notes of USD 1,000.0 million due 2031, USD 770.0 million due 2033 and USD 630.0 million due 2035 (Documentary Fact). Balance sheet response is the fourth: Kodiak issued USD 836.1 million of equity alongside a debt-financed acquisition (Documentary Fact), which is documented equity support. Secured debt is the fifth: only the USD 380.9 million drawn on the ABL is secured, equal to 0.50x LTM adjusted EBITDA on this analysis (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only because the covenant definition of senior secured debt is not supplied).

Weaknesses. Growth spending against cash flow is the first: commitments of USD 2.5 billion and guidance that implies negative free cash flow in 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings quality is the second: add-backs of 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA and weaker cash conversion of 62.5% (Documentary Fact and Calculated). Concentration is the third: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford, four customers at about 32% of revenue and one at 14%, and dependence on a limited number of suppliers (Documentary Fact). Power visibility is the fourth: one disclosed lease agreement, so most power revenue is Not disclosed in contract terms, and a power fleet utilisation of 89.6% in its first quarter (Documentary Fact; the conclusion that visibility is thin is Analyst Interpretation). Covenant opacity is the fifth: the maximum Leverage Ratio of 5.25 to 1.00 printed in the annual report is on a defined basis not supplied, and the amended calculation applied only through June 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact; headroom is Insufficient Information). Unquantified contingencies are the sixth: a sanctions-related payments matter with no estimated penalty and a sales tax liability disclosed on two bases (Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transaction that matters most is the acquisition of Distributed Power Solutions, LLC, a provider of turnkey distributed and behind-the-meter power generation, by Kodiak Gas Services, LLC. The type is an acquisition of 100% of the equity interests for cash and registrant shares. Signing was on February 5, 2026 at a value of approximately $675.0 million at signing, comprising $575.0 million of cash and 2,401,278 shares valued at approximately $100.0 million on a $41.64 five-day average price, with a $37.1 million termination fee payable by the registrant in certain circumstances (10-K pages 25 and 139). Closing was April 1, 2026 on cash of $587.3 million, adjusted for additional power generation assets bought before closing, indebtedness and working capital, and 2.4 million shares with an estimated fair value of $139.0 million at the $57.90 closing price, so the fair value of consideration transferred was 726,354 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 12 and 13; 10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24). The sellers are not named in the acquisition note; the registration rights agreement entered at closing names Mustang PRS, LLC and Louisiana Machinery Company, L.L.C. as holders of the registrant shares issued in the transaction (10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24); the pack does not otherwise name the sellers. The purchase price allocation is preliminary and recognises goodwill of 344,782 thousand USD, all in the Power Infrastructure reporting unit (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 13 and 19). The pack contains no bridge between the signing and closing values, so the difference is logged as a conflict below and not reconciled. The stated rationale, which is management language, is to expand beyond contract compression into distributed power generation and enhance revenue growth through scale and complementary services (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 12). Liquidity effect and use of proceeds: the notes and equity transactions that followed are described below; the pack does not state which source funded which part of the cash consideration, and the financial handoff shows cash paid net of cash acquired of 575,965 thousand USD in the first half of 2026. The status is complete, with the allocation open for up to one year from closing.

New debt in the period. On March 20, 2026 Kodiak Services issued $1.0 billion of 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031, with fees of $14.3 million, and used a portion of the net proceeds to redeem all $750.0 million of its 7.25% notes due 2029 at 103.625 percent, through a defeasance on March 30, 2026 that required a $785.5 million cash outlay and produced a loss on extinguishment of 36,512 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 21 to 23). The 2029 notes were redeemed April 10, 2026. On April 2, 2026 Kodiak and Kodiak Services signed the Fifth Amendment to the ABL credit agreement, which modifies the leverage ratio calculation by allowing net proceeds of the 2031 notes to be deducted from total indebtedness, in addition to the $50.0 million cash netting cap, through June 30, 2026 (page 21). In the prior year, on September 5, 2025 Kodiak Services issued $600.0 million each of 6.50% notes due 2033 and 6.75% notes due 2035, with add-ons of $170.0 million and $30.0 million on September 22, 2025, using the proceeds to repay part of the ABL, and a Fourth Amendment to the ABL reduced commitments to $2.0 billion and extended maturity to September 2030 (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 23; 10-K page 72), the amendment date not being stated in the text read. The equity side: an underwritten offering of 10.6 million shares at $71.00, with a further 1.6 million shares under the option, closed May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 26). The pack does not state a use of proceeds for that offering, and the financial handoff shows ABL drawings fell in the quarter; the link is an inference, not a documented fact. After quarter end Kodiak exercised options to buy about 43,000 horsepower of leased compression equipment for about $32.8 million in July 2026 and declared a $0.49 per share dividend on August 5, 2026 (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 29 and 35). The financial handoff carries the resulting leverage, liquidity and maturity figures: total debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA of 3.63x, liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m, and purchase commitments of $2.5 billion. Parties, status and amounts above are Documentary Facts; the stated rationales are Management Language; the possible link between the equity offering and ABL repayment is Analyst Interpretation.

fields.value: - Leverage and covenant evidence. The annual report prints the ABL tests ("The maximum Leverage Ratio is 5.25 to 1.00", a secured leverage maximum of 3.25 to 1.00 and "a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.5x", 10-K page:72). fields.value: The financial base is adequate for a bounded credit snapshot at the June 30, 2026 balance sheet date, with metrics that must be read as adjusted-EBITDA, principal-debt measures built from filed statements and company reconciliations. On those measures leverage has stepped down since December 2024: total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 4.31x at FY2024, 3.66x at FY2025, 3.92x on LTM March 2026 (when the notes refinancing had raised principal debt before the acquisition closed and before the May equity offering) and 3.63x on LTM June 2026. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 4.14x on LTM June 2026. Secured debt is small, because only the ABL is secured, and the next maturity of size is the ABL in 2030, followed by the unsecured notes from 2031. Three features temper that picture: the acquired power business contributes earnings only from April 1, 2026, so LTM EBITDA understates a full-year perimeter against debt and equity that already include its financing; operating cash conversion weakened in the first half of 2026; and purchase commitments rose sharply while guidance implies negative free cash flow in 2026. fields.value: Module: business and transaction context for Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. (issuer id kgs, NYSE: KGS), pathway credit_snapshot, as-of date 2026-11-05, evidence cutoff 2026-11-05, reporting currency USD. Current period q2-2026 (three and six months ended June 30, 2026); prior period fy-2025. Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor? Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. This handoff gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. External material is not used; every fact is from the pinned sources, and financial figures are carried from the financial-base handoff by its own labels. Each fact row below carries one of four categories: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kodiak's credit story is a contract compression operator with fixed-fee, multi-year contracts, high fleet utilisation and customers described as large upstream and midstream companies, that is in the middle of a strategic widening into distributed power. On the evidence, the compression core is stable and gaining visibility: remaining performance obligations rose sharply in the second quarter of 2026 and utilisation was 98.2%. The power build is the new variable. The acquisition closed on April 1, 2026, the acquired business has produced one quarter of results, only one customer lease is disclosed in detail, and purchase commitments rose to $2.5 billion. The financial handoff shows an equity offering, a refinanced notes stack and a largely undrawn ABL alongside this growth, which supports near-term liquidity but moves the credit from a steady-state contract business toward a capital-intensive build in which the pace of customer contracting, not demand commentary, matters. Ownership is public: the former sponsor affiliate exited in 2025, so no sponsor is documented as supporting or controlling the credit. Documented capital allocation shows both shareholder distributions and equity issuance; no priming, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is documented in the pack. Governance evidence is limited to filing summaries because the proxy statement and executed financing documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction that matters most is the acquisition of Distributed Power Solutions, LLC, a provider of turnkey distributed and behind-the-meter power generation, by Kodiak Gas Services, LLC. The type is an acquisition of 100% of the equity interests for cash and registrant shares. Signing was on February 5, 2026 at a value of approximately $675.0 million at signing, comprising $575.0 million of cash and 2,401,278 shares valued at approximately $100.0 million on a $41.64 five-day average price, with a $37.1 million termination fee payable by the registrant in certain circumstances (10-K pages 25 and 139). Closing was April 1, 2026 on cash of $587.3 million, adjusted for additional power generation assets bought before closing, indebtedness and working capital, and 2.4 million shares with an estimated fair value of $139.0 million at the $57.90 closing price, so the fair value of consideration transferred was 726,354 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 12 and 13; 10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24). The sellers are not named in the acquisition note; the registration rights agreement entered at closing names Mustang PRS, LLC and Louisiana Machinery Company, L.L.C. as holders of the registrant shares issued in the transaction (10-Q 2026-03-31 page 24); the pack does not otherwise name the sellers. The purchase price allocation is preliminary and recognises goodwill of 344,782 thousand USD, all in the Power Infrastructure reporting unit (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 13 and 19). The pack contains no bridge between the signing and closing values, so the difference is logged as a conflict below and not reconciled. The stated rationale, which is management language, is to expand beyond contract compression into distributed power generation and enhance revenue growth through scale and complementary services (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 12). Liquidity effect and use of proceeds: the notes and equity transactions that followed are described below; the pack does not state which source funded which part of the cash consideration, and the financial handoff shows cash paid net of cash acquired of 575,965 thousand USD in the first half of 2026. The status is complete, with the allocation open for up to one year from closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in the period. On March 20, 2026 Kodiak Services issued $1.0 billion of 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031, with fees of $14.3 million, and used a portion of the net proceeds to redeem all $750.0 million of its 7.25% notes due 2029 at 103.625 percent, through a defeasance on March 30, 2026 that required a $785.5 million cash outlay and produced a loss on extinguishment of 36,512 thousand USD (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 21 to 23). The 2029 notes were redeemed April 10, 2026. On April 2, 2026 Kodiak and Kodiak Services signed the Fifth Amendment to the ABL credit agreement, which modifies the leverage ratio calculation by allowing net proceeds of the 2031 notes to be deducted from total indebtedness, in addition to the $50.0 million cash netting cap, through June 30, 2026 (page 21). In the prior year, on September 5, 2025 Kodiak Services issued $600.0 million each of 6.50% notes due 2033 and 6.75% notes due 2035, with add-ons of $170.0 million and $30.0 million on September 22, 2025, using the proceeds to repay part of the ABL, and a Fourth Amendment to the ABL reduced commitments to $2.0 billion and extended maturity to September 2030 (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 23; 10-K page 72), the amendment date not being stated in the text read. The equity side: an underwritten offering of 10.6 million shares at $71.00, with a further 1.6 million shares under the option, closed May 15, 2026 for net proceeds of approximately $836.1 million (10-Q 2026-06-30 page 26). The pack does not state a use of proceeds for that offering, and the financial handoff shows ABL drawings fell in the quarter; the link is an inference, not a documented fact. After quarter end Kodiak exercised options to buy about 43,000 horsepower of leased compression equipment for about $32.8 million in July 2026 and declared a $0.49 per share dividend on August 5, 2026 (10-Q 2026-06-30 pages 29 and 35). The financial handoff carries the resulting leverage, liquidity and maturity figures: total debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA of 3.63x, liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m, and purchase commitments of $2.5 billion. Parties, status and amounts above are Documentary Facts; the stated rationales are Management Language; the possible link between the equity offering and ABL repayment is Analyst Interpretation.

fields.value: 1. Revenue durability (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: fixed monthly fees with primary terms of one to seven years (10-K page:16), 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and performance obligations of 2,643,245 thousand USD at June 30, 2026 against LTM compression revenue of 1,220,890 thousand USD (Calculation A2). Mechanic: take-or-pay-style fees convert fleet utilisation into near-term revenue regardless of volumes, and the rise in obligations extends the contracted period. Implication: supports near-term revenue visibility and debt service; the step up is unexplained, and the tail beyond 2027 was thin until the second quarter. Counter: the shorter-term tail and month-to-month contracts are the exposure if basin activity weakens.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: Compression adjusted gross margin of 70.0% in the second quarter against Other Services at 11.3%, below 15.9% in the first quarter of 2026 and 24.5% a year earlier (release 2026-08-06 page:6), with receivables and working capital absorbing cash in the first half (financial handoff, cash flow quality). Mechanic: the high-margin compression stream carries the credit; Other Services margin erosion and working capital drag reduce cash conversion. Implication: credit metrics on adjusted EBITDA overstate cash earnings in 2026; the financial handoff shows operating cash flow at 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration risk (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford (10-K page:13), four largest customers about 32% of revenue and one customer 14%, and a limited number of suppliers. Mechanic: basin activity, a single large customer's decisions and equipment lead times drive utilisation and growth timing. Implication: loss of the largest customer or a supplier disruption would have a disproportionate effect on utilisation and growth timing; no peer comparison is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Transformation and execution risk in power (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: one disclosed lease with initial term to April 1, 2028, revised power growth capital spending guidance, purchase commitments of $2.5 billion against $276.4 million at March 31, 2026 (10-Q 2026-03-31 page:34), and a one gigawatt turbine order (release 2026-08-06 page:2). Mechanic: equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, so cash is committed ahead of revenue; power lease revenue was 8.4% of second quarter revenue (Calculation A3). Implication: liquidity of 1,742.0 US$m in the financial handoff must absorb a 12-month commitment of $587.9 million plus negative implied free cash flow; delays in contracting would raise leverage because EBITDA from the new assets lags the financing. Counter: management states customer discussions are advanced, a Management Language claim that is not backed by executed contracts in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Sponsor alignment (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: the sponsor affiliate holding fell to zero by December 2, 2025 with no proceeds to Kodiak. Mechanic: with no sponsor, distributions and acquisitions are decided by a public-company board under the covenant package; ABL-funded dividends require $100,000,000 pro forma availability. fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis of Kodiak Gas Services, Inc. (KGS), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, latest balance sheet date June 30, 2026. It uses only the settled financial-base and business-context handoffs. Scope is business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source page was read again for this module; every fact below comes from the handoffs listed next, which cite these sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kodiak Gas Services is a moderately leveraged contract compression credit whose strength is contracted, high-margin revenue and ample liquidity, and whose main exposure is a power build financed ahead of contracts. Compression remaining performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, utilisation of 98.2% and total debt of 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA after an equity raise of USD 836.1 million support the credit, with liquidity of USD 1,742.0 million and no scheduled debt maturity of size before 2030. The weakest point is that growth spending outruns cash generation: purchase commitments are USD 2.5 billion, guidance implies negative 2026 free cash flow, and only one power lease is disclosed. Delivery of power contracts against that spending, and covenant headroom that cannot be recomputed here, decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kodiak's cash-generative, contracted compression fleet and equity-supported balance sheet carry the credit through a power build whose repayment capacity is not yet evidenced by contracts (Analyst Interpretation, resting on the contract, leverage and commitment rows below).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first finding is revenue durability. Kodiak sells compression on fixed monthly fees under primary terms of one to seven years, with 9.0% of revenue-generating horsepower on month-to-month terms, and its compression remaining performance obligations were USD 2,643.2 million at June 30, 2026 against USD 1,632.9 million at March 31, 2026, with 49.9% falling in 2028 or later (Documentary Fact, from the business-context handoff). The mechanism is that fixed fees turn 98.2% utilisation into revenue largely independent of volume, so contracted obligations of 2.17 times LTM compression revenue protect near-term coverage of debt service. The implication is stronger revenue visibility than the previous quarter showed, tempered because the filings do not explain the jump and the month-to-month tail would reprice quickly in a weak basin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second is financial risk and leverage. Total debt was USD 2,780.9 million, or 3.63x LTM adjusted EBITDA of USD 766.1 million, and net debt was 3.45x, against 4.31x total and 4.30x net at FY2024 and 3.66x total at FY2025 (Documentary Fact for inputs, Calculated in the financial-base handoff). The mechanism is that the May equity offering of USD 836.1 million arrived in the same period as the USD 576.0 million cash acquisition and a notes refinancing, so debt rose by USD 166.3 million since December 2025 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 51.1 million. The implication for leverage tolerance is a stepped-down but not yet clearly falling ratio; the figure overstates leverage on a full-year perimeter because EBITDA from the acquired power business before April 1, 2026 is Not calculable, and management's covenant-basis ratio of 3.2x (Management Language) cannot be recomputed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third is funding and liquidity. Liquidity was USD 1,742.0 million (cash of USD 137.6 million and undrawn ABL capacity of USD 1,604.5 million, an upper bound because the borrowing base is not supplied), against purchase commitments of USD 2.5 billion, of which USD 587.9 million is expected within twelve months, up from USD 276.4 million at March 31, 2026. Revised 2026 guidance implies discretionary cash flow less growth and other capital spending of negative USD 235.0 million to negative USD 125.0 million, before dividends of about USD 49.5 million a quarter. The mechanism is that the spending is discretionary in timing but contractually committed once ordered, and the ABL, which matures September 5, 2030 and is secured on essentially all assets, is the funding backstop. The implication is that refinancing risk is low through 2029 but that net leverage, on the indicative sensitivity below, ends 2026 at about 3.27x to 3.52x, roughly where it is today, unless adjusted EBITDA beats guidance or equity is raised again (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth is earnings and cash quality. Add-backs were USD 162.7 million, or 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA, and unadjusted leverage on the same debt would be 4.61x; operating cash flow was 62.5% of LTM adjusted EBITDA against 83.9% in FY2025, as working capital used USD 154.6 million in the first half (Documentary Fact and Calculated). The mechanism is that equity compensation, a settled sales tax reserve and refinancing and acquisition costs sit outside adjusted EBITDA while the sales tax settlement and working capital absorbed cash. The implication is that adjusted-EBITDA coverage of 4.14x on cash interest paid is a ceiling on debt-service capacity, and monitoring should use operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth is the power transition and ownership. The acquisition closed April 1, 2026 with fair value of consideration of USD 726.4 million (signing value was about USD 675.0 million, logged as a conflict, not reconciled), goodwill of USD 344.8 million on a preliminary allocation, one disclosed lease agreement whose initial term ends April 1, 2028, and no sponsor, since EQT affiliates sold their entire stake by December 2, 2025 (Documentary Fact). The mechanism is that equipment is bought before multi-year contracts are shown, and no sponsor is documented as available to cure a shortfall. The implication is that the next two to three quarters of power contract announcements and utilisation are the main evidence that will move the credit view either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Contracted revenue visibility is the first: fixed-fee compression contracts, 98.2% utilisation, performance obligations of USD 2,643.2 million, and customer cost pass-throughs for fuel and taxes (Documentary Fact; business-context handoff). Margin resilience is the second: compression adjusted gross margin was 70.0% in the second quarter and adjusted EBITDA margin was 55.4% (Documentary Fact; financial-base handoff), which cushions a revenue decline. Liquidity and maturity profile is the third: USD 1,742.0 million of liquidity, no scheduled maturity of size before the ABL in 2030, and notes of USD 1,000.0 million due 2031, USD 770.0 million due 2033 and USD 630.0 million due 2035 (Documentary Fact). Balance sheet response is the fourth: Kodiak issued USD 836.1 million of equity alongside a debt-financed acquisition (Documentary Fact), which is documented equity support. Secured debt is the fifth: only the USD 380.9 million drawn on the ABL is secured, equal to 0.50x LTM adjusted EBITDA on this analysis (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only because the covenant definition of senior secured debt is not supplied).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Growth spending against cash flow is the first: commitments of USD 2.5 billion and guidance that implies negative free cash flow in 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings quality is the second: add-backs of 21.2% of LTM adjusted EBITDA and weaker cash conversion of 62.5% (Documentary Fact and Calculated). Concentration is the third: 82.8% of compression assets in the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford, four customers at about 32% of revenue and one at 14%, and dependence on a limited number of suppliers (Documentary Fact). Power visibility is the fourth: one disclosed lease agreement, so most power revenue is Not disclosed in contract terms, and a power fleet utilisation of 89.6% in its first quarter (Documentary Fact; the conclusion that visibility is thin is Analyst Interpretation). Covenant opacity is the fifth: the maximum Leverage Ratio of 5.25 to 1.00 printed in the annual report is on a defined basis not supplied, and the amended calculation applied only through June 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact; headroom is Insufficient Information). Unquantified contingencies are the sixth: a sanctions-related payments matter with no estimated penalty and a sales tax liability disclosed on two bases (Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four items should be tracked each quarter, in this order: free cash flow against the USD 587.9 million of twelve-month commitments and the ABL balance; announcements of signed power leases and power utilisation against the 89.6% first-quarter level; the covenant leverage ratio and any amended terms, once the credit agreement is supplied; and conversion of performance obligations, to see whether the second-quarter jump reflects durable new contracts.
